title: GPSR Requirements for Online Product Listings: What Your Product Data Needs
summary: GPSR requires every EU online listing to show manufacturer details, product identifiers and safety warnings. See what each listing needs and how to keep it complete.
body_markdown:
The EU's General Product Safety Regulation (GPSR) requires every consumer product sold online in the EU to show safety and traceability details on the listing itself. That means the manufacturer's contact details, an EU responsible person when the manufacturer is outside the EU, information that identifies the product, and any warnings or safety information in the shopper's language.


For a retailer or brand selling into the EU, each of those is a field in the product record that has to be filled for every product and kept in sync with every channel. This guide covers what a listing needs, which products are exempt and how to keep the data complete across a large catalog.


It covers the product data side of GPSR. Check your legal obligations with your own counsel.


## What is GPSR?


GPSR is[Regulation (EU) 2023/988](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2023/988/oj/eng) , the EU law that sets general safety rules for consumer products. It has applied since 13 December 2024 and replaced the earlier General Product Safety Directive.


It covers products sold to consumers in the EU, whether new, used, repaired or reconditioned, and whether they're sold in a store or online. Products covered by sector-specific EU safety rules, such as toys, follow those rules for the risks they cover, and GPSR applies to the rest.


## What information does GPSR require on an online product listing?


Article 19 says that when a product is sold online, the offer must "clearly and visibly" show at least four things:


1. **The manufacturer.** Its name, registered trade name or registered trademark, plus a postal address and an electronic address, such as an email or contact form, where it can be reached.
2. **The EU responsible person, when the manufacturer is outside the EU.** Their name, postal address and electronic address.
3. **Information that identifies the product.** This includes a picture of the product, its type and any other product identifier, such as a model or batch number.
4. **Warnings and safety information.** Any warning or safety information that has to appear on the product, its packaging or an accompanying document, in a language consumers in that country can easily understand.


Online marketplaces have a matching duty. Article 22 requires them to give sellers a way to enter this information for each product and to show it on the product listing.


### What this means for your product record


Each requirement maps to data you hold, or should hold, for every SKU:


GPSR requirement Product data it needs


Manufacturer details Manufacturer name and trademark, postal address, email or contact URL


EU responsible person Name, postal address and electronic address, for products made outside the EU


Product identification Product images, product type, and identifiers such as model number, batch number or GTIN


Warnings and safety information Warning text and safety instructions, translated into the language of each market you sell in


The manufacturer and responsible person usually stay the same across a brand's products, so they can be set once per brand. Warnings vary by product and by language, which makes them the hardest part to keep complete.


## Which products are exempt from GPSR?


GPSR lists the products it doesn't apply to. These include medicinal products for human or veterinary use, food, feed, living plants and animals, animal by-products, plant protection products and antiques. It also excludes some transport equipment that a service provider operates for consumers, and certain aircraft.


Most other consumer products sold online fall under it, including clothing, furniture, electronics, toys and cosmetics. Some of these also have their own EU rules, which apply alongside GPSR.


## How do you add GPSR information on Shopify and marketplaces?


On Shopify, the[GPSR help page](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/international/gpsr) points merchants to its Disclosures feature for legally required product warnings, which uses a product metafield. Other required details can go in the product description or a custom metafield.


Marketplaces each provide their own fields for GPSR details, as Article 22 requires. The field names and formats differ between marketplaces, so the same manufacturer and warning data has to be mapped to each one.


When GPSR details are typed into each channel by hand, the same information ends up in several places. Storing it once in the product record and sending it to every channel keeps the storefront and the marketplaces in step when a warning or an address changes.


## How do you manage GPSR compliance across a large catalog?


Treat each GPSR requirement as attributes in your product record, then check those attributes like any other required data before a product goes live in an EU market.


### Collect the data from suppliers and labels


Manufacturer details and warnings are usually already on the product's packaging or in its manual and the supplier's spec sheet. The work is getting them into structured fields instead of leaving them in PDFs and images. Ask suppliers to send them as fields in their product data, and fill the gaps from documents for products already in your catalog.


### Check completeness before publishing


Set a rule that a product can't go live in an EU market until its GPSR fields are filled: manufacturer, responsible person where needed, identifiers, images and warnings in that market's language. Run the same check whenever a product's data changes, so an updated warning or address doesn't leave a gap.


### Translate warnings for each market


Article 19 requires warnings in a language consumers in each country can easily understand. A product sold in France and Germany needs its warnings in French and German, so warnings belong in your translation workflow alongside the rest of the listing.

## Frequently asked questions


### Is GPSR being enforced?


Yes. GPSR has applied since 13 December 2024, and market surveillance authorities in each EU country enforce it. Online marketplaces also have their own obligations under the regulation, including making sellers' GPSR information visible on listings.
